description: Priority 1: grossly fragmented, discontinuous, or severely irregular anchored object; assign before every other phenotype and independently of viability signal
Priority 2: at least two distinct nuclei within the anchored object, only when Priority 1 is absent; use the Nuclei display as review evidence
Priority 3: dominantly enlarged, spread, or flattened morphology, only when Priorities 1-2 are absent
Priority 4: dominantly rounded and compact morphology, only when Priorities 1-3 are absent
Priority 5: exactly one evident nucleus and no morphology defined by Priorities 1-4
Priority 6: countable anchored morphology that is reviewable but matches none of Priorities 1-5
Nontrainable: insufficient image or mask evidence to apply the priority tree; do not infer a viability class
